$comment: Findings the release gate does not block on, each with a reason and a date it stops applying.
An entry belongs here only when the fix cannot be obtained from this repository: code vendored
inside the base image's own binaries, where the image vendor is the only party who can ship it.
A package this repository installs is never allowlisted; it is bumped.
Every entry prints on every run, an expired entry fails the build, and an entry that matches
nothing prints as stale. scripts/check-image-scan.mjs enforces all three.

OpenSSL statically linked inside the Node binary in node:22-slim. Inspector reports the fix as OpenSSL 4.0.2; no Node 22 image ships it, so nothing in this repository can obtain it. Clears when the Node image rebases onto a fixed OpenSSL, or when the runtime moves to a Node major that bundles 4.x.

OpenSSL 3.5.7 statically linked inside the Node binary in node:22-slim, at /usr/local/include/node/openssl/. Inspector reports the fix as OpenSSL 4.0.2; no Node 22 image ships it, so nothing in this repository can obtain it. This one reads fixAvailable PARTIAL on the backend image, because Debian's own openssl 3.0.20 is implicated there too and has no fix at all — and YES on the frontend, whose apt upgrade left only the vendored copy. Same unreachable fix either way; the gate only sees the difference. Clears when the Node image rebases onto a fixed OpenSSL, or when the runtime moves to a Node major that bundles 4.x.
